BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the basis of division first. 2) the tree from the top down. 3) each kind with its identifying feature and an example. 4) the borderline cases and exceptions. 5) the tree as recap.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

p001-i14 | 1 | table_row | comparison | 1) Mitosis: It occurs in somatic cells. | Meiosis: It occurs in germ cells.
  p001-i14#q1 | compare | Which cell categories does the table associate with the two divisions? → It associates mitosis with somatic cells and meiosis with germ cells. | book
  p001-i14#q2 | difference | What is the distinction between somatic and germ cells? → Somatic cells are body cells outside the reproductive germ line; germ-line cells give rise to reproductive cells. | outside
  p001-i14#q3 | why | Why must this row be treated as a simplified association? → Germ-line cells can also multiply by mitosis. In plants, meiosis produces spores in spore mother cells, so the row is not a complete description of every life cycle. | outside
p001-i15 | 1 | table_row | comparison | 2) Mitosis: Nucleus divides only once. | Meiosis: Nucleus divides twice.
  p001-i15#q1 | compare | How many nuclear divisions occur in each? → Mitosis has one nuclear division; meiosis has two. | book
  p001-i15#q2 | difference | What are the two meiotic divisions called? → They are meiosis I and meiosis II. | outside
  p001-i15#q3 | how | How do the two meiotic divisions accomplish different separations? → Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes, whereas meiosis II separates sister chromatids. | outside
p001-i16 | 1 | table_row | comparison | 3) Mitosis: Two daughter cells are formed. | Meiosis: Four daughter cells are formed.
  p001-i16#q1 | compare | What daughter-cell counts are printed? → The table gives two for mitosis and four for meiosis. | book
  p001-i16#q2 | difference | How do these outcomes differ? → The typical meiotic outcome has twice as many products as a single mitotic division. | book
  p001-i16#q3 | how | How does the division pattern account for the counts? → One division usually gives two products; in meiosis, both products of the first division undergo a second division, giving four. Unequal cytokinesis in animal egg formation means these are not four equivalent functional eggs. | outside
p001-i17 | 1 | table_row | comparison | 4) Mitosis: Daughter cells are diploid. | Meiosis: Daughter cells are haploid.
  p001-i17#q1 | compare | What ploidy does the table assign to the daughter cells? → It describes mitotic daughters as diploid and meiotic daughters as haploid. | book
  p001-i17#q2 | difference | How do diploid and haploid differ? → Diploid means two chromosome sets, written 2n; haploid means one set, written n. These symbols describe chromosome sets and have no physical unit. | outside
  p001-i17#q3 | why | Why does the mitosis statement require a starting-cell qualification? → Mitosis generally preserves the starting ploidy. A diploid parent gives diploid daughters, but a haploid cell can also divide mitotically and produce haploid daughters. | outside
p001-i18 | 1 | table_row | comparison | 5) Mitosis: It occurs more frequently. | Meiosis: It occurs less frequently.
  p001-i18#q1 | compare | How does the table compare frequency? → It calls mitosis more frequent and meiosis less frequent. | book
  p001-i18#q2 | difference | Does this row provide a numerical frequency difference? → No. It states a qualitative contrast without counts, rates or a specified organism. | book
  p001-i18#q3 | why | Why is mitosis often more widespread in a growing multicellular organism? → Growth and cell replacement require repeated divisions in many tissues, whereas meiosis is restricted to particular reproductive cells and stages. Actual frequencies depend on the organism, tissue and life stage. | outside
p001-i19 | 1 | table_row | comparison | 6) Mitosis: Daughter cells form somatic organs. | Meiosis: Daughter cells form gametes.
  p001-i19#q1 | compare | What roles does the row assign to the products? → Mitotic daughter cells contribute to somatic organs, while meiotic daughter cells are associated with gamete formation. | book
  p001-i19#q2 | difference | How do these roles differ? → The row contrasts body formation with reproductive-cell formation. | book
  p001-i19#q3 | how | How should the gamete statement be qualified for plants? → In land plants, meiosis produces haploid spores. These develop into gametophytes that produce gametes through mitosis; meiotic products are therefore not universally gametes. | outside
p001-i20 | 1 | table_row | comparison | 7) Mitosis: There is only one prophase, one metaphase one anaphase and one telophase. | Meiosis: There are two of each phase and five sub-phases in prophase - 1.
  p001-i20#q1 | compare | How does the table compare the division phases? → Mitosis has one occurrence of each named phase; meiosis has two, with five sub-phases in prophase I. | book
  p001-i20#q2 | difference | Which phase has the additional subdivision highlighted here? → Prophase I of meiosis has five sub-phases. | book
  p001-i20#q3 | how | How do the phases organise chromosome separation? → Chromosomes condense during prophase, align during metaphase, separate during anaphase and reach the poles as division concludes in telophase. Prophase I includes homologous pairing and crossing over; its five standard sub-phases are leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis. | outside
p001-i21 | 1 | table_row | comparison | 8) Mitosis: Number of chromosomes are not changed in the daughter cells. | Meiosis: Number of chromosomes are reduced to half.
  p001-i21#q1 | compare | How do daughter-cell chromosome numbers compare with the starting cell? → Mitosis preserves the number, while meiosis reduces it to half. | book
  p001-i21#q2 | difference | Which process is associated with chromosome-number reduction? → Meiosis is the reductional process in this comparison. | book
  p001-i21#q3 | how | How is chromosome number halved in meiosis? → Homologous partners separate into different cells in meiosis I, leaving one member of each pair in each product. Meiosis II then separates sister chromatids without a further halving of chromosome sets. | outside
p001-i22 | 1 | table_row | comparison | 9) Mitosis: Chromosome number doubles at the beginning of each cell division. | Meiosis: Chromosome number is not doubled. It doubles after the end of first meiotic division.
  p001-i22#q1 | compare | What timing claims does the printed row make? → It claims chromosome number doubles at the beginning of mitotic division and after the first meiotic division. These are the printed claims, not reliable statements of the mechanism. | book
  p001-i22#q2 | difference | What distinction is needed to evaluate this row? → Chromosome number and DNA amount differ. DNA replication creates sister chromatids while chromosome number, conventionally counted by centromeres, remains unchanged before their separation. | outside
  p001-i22#q3 | how | How does DNA replication actually relate to mitosis and meiosis? → DNA replicates in S phase before mitosis and before meiosis I. There is no intervening S phase of DNA replication between meiosis I and meiosis II. The printed row confuses chromosome number, DNA replication and its timing. | outside
  p001-i22#q4 | why | Why is the claimed doubling after meiosis I especially misleading? → Meiosis depends on one replication followed by two divisions. Replicating the genome again between those divisions would not describe the standard meiotic sequence. | outside
p001-i23 | 1 | table_row | comparison | 10) Mitosis: No crossing over in chromosomes. | Meiosis: Crossing over occurs chromosomes.
  p001-i23#q1 | compare | How does the table contrast crossing over? → It presents crossing over as absent in mitosis and present in meiosis. | book
  p001-i23#q2 | difference | What does crossing over involve in the standard meiotic account? → It involves exchange of corresponding DNA segments between non-sister chromatids of paired homologous chromosomes during prophase I. | outside
  p001-i23#q3 | why | Why is crossing over significant? → It creates new combinations of alleles on chromosomes and helps establish connections important for homologous chromosome segregation. Rare mitotic recombination means the printed absence should be understood as the usual introductory contrast. | outside
p001-i24 | 1 | table_row | comparison | 11) Mitosis: Equation division. | Meiosis: Reduction division.
  p001-i24#q1 | compare | Which division labels are printed? → The table prints 'Equation division' for mitosis and 'Reduction division' for meiosis. | book
  p001-i24#q2 | difference | What is the intended distinction between these terms? → The standard term for mitosis is equational division: chromosome sets are preserved. Meiosis is reductional overall because chromosome sets are halved. | outside
  p001-i24#q3 | why | Why should the two meiotic divisions be distinguished here? → Meiosis I is reductional because homologues separate; meiosis II is equational because sister chromatids separate. Calling meiosis reduction division describes its overall outcome. | outside
p001-i26 | 1 | table_row | comparison | Plants: Centrioles are absent. | Animals: Centrioles are present.
  p001-i26#q1 | compare | How does the table compare centrioles? → It describes centrioles as absent in plants and present in animals. | book
  p001-i26#q2 | difference | Which side of the comparison is associated with centrioles? → The animal side. | book
  p001-i26#q3 | how | How can plant cells divide without the animal-type centriole arrangement? → Their spindle microtubules can be organised without centriole-containing centrosomes. The printed contrast fits typical higher-plant and animal cells; some plant groups have centrioles or related basal bodies in particular cells. | outside
p001-i27 | 1 | table_row | comparison | Plants: Asters are not formed. | Animals: Asters are formed.
  p001-i27#q1 | compare | What does the table state about asters? → Asters are not formed in plant mitosis but are formed in animal mitosis. | book
  p001-i27#q2 | difference | What is an aster in this comparison? → An aster is a star-like array of microtubules radiating from a centrosomal region in a dividing cell. | outside
  p001-i27#q3 | why | Why is the aster difference related to the preceding row? → Typical animal centrosomes organise astral microtubules, whereas typical higher-plant cells organise their mitotic spindle without that centrosome-and-aster arrangement. | outside
p001-i28 | 1 | table_row | comparison | Plants: Cell division involves formation of a cell plate. | Animals: Cell division involves furrowing and cleavage of cytoplasm.
  p001-i28#q1 | compare | How does the table compare cytoplasmic division? → Plant cells form a cell plate; animal cells divide by furrowing and cleavage of the cytoplasm. | book
  p001-i28#q2 | difference | How do the directions of these mechanisms differ? → A plant cell plate develops centrally and expands outward; an animal cleavage furrow constricts inward from the cell surface. | outside
  p001-i28#q3 | why | Why do plant and animal cells use different mechanisms? → The rigid plant cell wall limits pinching, so vesicles build a partition between daughter cells. In animal cells, an actin–myosin contractile ring constricts the cell surface. | outside
  p001-i28#q4 | how | How is this distinct from division of the nucleus? → These mechanisms describe cytokinesis, which partitions cytoplasm; mitosis describes the nuclear division that distributes chromosomes. | outside
p001-i29 | 1 | table_row | comparison | Plants: Occurs mainly at meristem. | Animals: Occurs in tissues throughout the body.
  p001-i29#q1 | compare | Where does the table locate mitosis in plants and animals? → Mainly at meristems in plants, and in tissues throughout the body in animals. | book
  p001-i29#q2 | difference | What spatial contrast is being made? → Plant division is associated mainly with specialised growth regions, while animal division is described as distributed through body tissues. | book
  p001-i29#q3 | why | Why should 'throughout the body' not be read as every animal cell dividing? → Animal tissues differ in their capacity for division; some mature specialised cells have very limited division. Plant cells outside established meristems may also regain division capacity in suitable circumstances. | outside

  p001-i34#q3 | how | How can lateral meristems increase girth? → Cambial tissues produce new cells toward the inside or outside, adding tissue layers around the organ. | outside

  p001-i35#q2 | difference | How does intercalary meristem differ in position from apical meristem? → Intercalary meristems occur between more mature tissues, commonly near leaf bases or internode bases in grasses; apical meristems occur at growing tips. | outside
  p001-i35#q3 | how | How can intercalary meristems help grasses regrow after cutting? → Dividing cells at retained basal growth regions can continue producing new tissue even when upper portions have been removed. | outside

  p001-i37#q3 | why | Why are all three labels grouped under Simple? → Each is recognised as a tissue primarily characterised by one general type of cell, despite variations within that type. | outside

  p001-i38#q2 | difference | What distinguishes complex from simple permanent tissue? → Complex tissue contains different cell types working together, whereas simple tissue is mainly composed of one cell type. | outside
  p001-i38#q3 | how | How does the chart illustrate this complexity? → It lists several named components beneath each of Xylem and Phloem, showing that each includes multiple components. | book
p001-i39 | 1 | diagram_label | classification | Paranchyma: child of Simple under Permanent Tissue; spelling as printed.
  p001-i39#q1 | which | Which category contains the label Paranchyma? → Simple permanent tissue. | book
  p001-i39#q2 | difference | How does the tissue intended by this label differ from sclerenchyma? → The standard term is parenchyma. Its cells are generally living and have relatively thin primary walls; sclerenchyma commonly has thick lignified walls and cells dead at maturity. | outside
  p001-i39#q3 | how | How can parenchyma serve different functions? → Living cells can store materials, and chloroplast-containing forms can photosynthesise. Their functions depend on location and specialisation. | outside
p001-i40 | 1 | diagram_label | classification | Collenchyma: child of Simple under Permanent Tissue.
  p001-i40#q1 | which | Where is Collenchyma classified? → Under Simple permanent tissue. | book
  p001-i40#q2 | difference | How does collenchyma differ from parenchyma? → Collenchyma has living cells with unevenly thickened primary walls suited to support, whereas typical parenchyma has relatively thin primary walls. | outside
  p001-i40#q3 | how | How does collenchyma support growing parts? → Its thickened but flexible walls provide strength while allowing bending and continued growth in young organs. | outside
p001-i41 | 1 | diagram_label | classification | Sclerenchyma: child of Simple under Permanent Tissue; parent of Fibres and Sclereids.

  p001-i41#q3 | why | Why is sclerenchyma suited to mechanical strength? → Thick lignified walls resist deformation and reinforce mature plant parts. | outside
p001-i42 | 1 | diagram_label | classification | Fibres: child of Sclerenchyma.
  p001-i42#q1 | which | Which tissue is the parent of Fibres here? → Sclerenchyma. | book

  p001-i42#q3 | how | How do fibres strengthen plant parts? → Their elongated, thick-walled cells often occur in groups and help resist pulling and bending forces. | outside

  p001-i43#q3 | how | How do sclereids contribute to hardness? → Their thick lignified walls give local rigidity; stone cells in pear flesh provide a familiar example of their gritty texture. | outside

  p001-i47#q3 | how | How does living parenchyma contribute to xylem? → It stores materials and assists lateral movement and exchange of substances within the tissue. | outside
p001-i48 | 1 | diagram_label | classification | Phloem: child of Complex under Permanent Tissue. Visible listed components: Sieve tubes; Companion cells; Phloem parenchyma. Lower box edge is cropped.

p001-i49 | 1 | diagram_label | classification | Sieve tubes: listed component of Phloem.

  p001-i49#q3 | how | How do sieve tubes form a transport route? → Sieve-tube elements join end to end, with sieve-plate pores allowing phloem sap to pass between them. | outside

  p001-i50#q3 | why | Why are companion cells closely associated with sieve-tube elements? → They provide metabolic support and participate in loading, unloading and maintaining the conducting system through close cellular connections. | outside

p008-i10 | 8 | diagram | classification | Plant Tissues branches into Meristematic tissue and Permanent tissue. Meristematic tissue branches into Apical meristem, Intercalary meristem and Lateral meristem. Permanent tissue branches into Simple permanent tissue and Complex permanent tissue. Simple permanent tissue branches into Parenchyma, Collenchyma and Sclerenchyma. Parenchyma branches into Aerenchyma and Chlorenchyma. Sclerenchyma branches into Sclerenchyma fibers and Sclereids. beats.say: Plant की बढ़ती tip और मजबूत पुरानी stem में cells का काम एक जैसा क्यों नहीं होता? कहीं नए cells बनाने हैं, कहीं support देना है। आज division के differences से चलकर इन tissues का पूरा नक्शा जोड़ेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Growing tip and mature stem; division → tissue map.

beats.say: Mitosis और meiosis, दोनों में nucleus के chromosomes daughter cells तक पहुँचते हैं। तुलना में पहले cell का context, फिर divisions और products, फिर chromosome number देखेंगे। केवल 2 और 4 याद करना पूरी समझ नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Common feature: chromosome distribution; comparison criteria appear.

beats.say: Book mitosis को somatic cells, यानी body cells से, और meiosis को germ cells से जोड़ती है। Products के काम में mitosis से somatic organs बनते हैं; meiosis को gamete formation से जोड़ा गया है। इसे शुरुआती तुलना समझो, हर life cycle का पूरा नियम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Somatic cells/body formation ↔ germ cells/reproductive association.

beats.say: Mitosis में nucleus 1 बार divide होता है और आम तौर पर 2 daughter cells बनते हैं। Meiosis में 2 nuclear divisions, meiosis I और meiosis II, से आम तौर पर 4 products बनते हैं। यानी इस तुलना में meiotic products की गिनती दोगुनी है।
beats.on_screen: Mitosis: 1 → 2; meiosis: 1 → 2 → 4.

beats.say: Book mitotic daughters को diploid और meiotic daughters को haploid कहती है। Diploid में 2 chromosome sets, यानी 2n; haploid में 1 set, यानी n होता है। Mitosis में starting chromosome number बचता है, meiosis में आधा रह जाता है।
beats.on_screen: Diploid starting cell: mitosis 2n → 2n; meiosis 2n → n.

beats.say: Frequency में book mitosis को more frequent और meiosis को less frequent बताती है। कोई rate या numerical difference नहीं दिया है। Phases में mitosis का prophase, metaphase, anaphase और telophase 1-1 बार आता है; meiosis में हर phase 2 बार, और prophase I के 5 sub-phases हैं।
beats.on_screen: Qualitative frequency contrast; one phase sequence versus I and II; prophase I: 5 subdivisions.

beats.say: Crossing over को table mitosis में absent और meiosis में present दिखाती है। इसमें paired homologous chromosomes की non-sister chromatids के बीच corresponding DNA segments exchange होते हैं। यह meiosis के prophase I की घटना है, जिससे नए allele combinations बन सकते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Paired homologues exchange matching segments; introductory mitosis/meiosis contrast.

beats.say: इन differences की वजह separation का तरीका है। Meiosis I में homologous partners अलग होते हैं, इसलिए sets आधे होते हैं; meiosis II में sister chromatids अलग होती हैं। Mitosis starting ploidy बचाता है, इसलिए diploid parent से diploid, लेकिन haploid parent से haploid daughters भी बन सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Homologues separate in I; sister chromatids separate in II; mitosis preserves starting ploidy.

beats.say: Growth और cell replacement में बार-बार mitosis चाहिए; meiosis खास reproductive stages से जुड़ा है। Germ-line cells भी mitosis कर सकती हैं। Land plants में meiosis सीधे gametes नहीं, spores बनाता है; उनसे बने gametophytes mitosis से gametes बनाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Growth/replacement; land plants: meiosis → spores → gametophyte → gametes by mitosis.

beats.say: सबसे जरूरी confusion: chromosome number और DNA amount अलग हैं। Printed row mitosis की शुरुआत में chromosome doubling, और meiosis I के बाद doubling का दावा करती है; यह सही mechanism नहीं है। DNA S phase में mitosis से पहले और meiosis I से पहले copy होता है, meiosis I और II के बीच नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Printed row flagged incorrect; DNA replication → mitosis OR meiosis I → meiosis II, with no intervening replication.

beats.say: DNA copying से sister chromatids बनती हैं; centromeres से गिने जाने वाला chromosome number उसी समय दोगुना नहीं होता। Book का ‘Equation division’ standard term equational division के लिए है। Mitosis equational है; meiosis overall reduction division है, लेकिन meiosis I reductional और meiosis II equational है।
beats.on_screen: DNA amount ≠ chromosome number; Equation [printed] → equational [standard].

beats.say: Table को अब पढ़ो: mitosis में 1 division, 2 daughters, chromosome number वही; meiosis में 2 divisions, 4 products, number आधा। Phases का 1 set बनाम 2 sets, और usual crossing-over contrast भी साथ रखो। DNA replication वाली printed row को सही sequence से बदलकर समझना है।
beats.on_screen: Comparison table with all taught criteria; incorrect replication row replaced by corrected sequence.

beats.say: अब plant और animal cells की तुलना में दोनों तरफ mitosis ही है। दोनों को chromosomes बाँटने हैं और cytoplasm अलग करना है। Nucleus का division mitosis है; cytoplasm बाँटना cytokinesis है।
beats.on_screen: Shared tasks: nuclear division and cytokinesis, labelled separately.

beats.say: Table में plants की तरफ centrioles absent, animals की तरफ present हैं। Asters भी plants में नहीं, animals में बनते हैं। Aster को centrosomal region से फैलती star-like microtubules की arrangement समझो।
beats.on_screen: Typical plant versus animal spindle; animal centriole and aster highlighted.

beats.say: Cytokinesis में plant cell cell plate बनाता है; animal cell में furrowing और cytoplasm का cleavage होता है। Division की जगह भी अलग दिखाई गई है: plants में mainly meristem, animals में body के अलग-अलग tissues। Mainly का मतलब केवल वहीं नहीं, और throughout का मतलब हर cell नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Cell plate ↔ cleavage furrow; meristems ↔ distributed dividing tissues.

beats.say: Typical higher-plant cells centrioles वाले centrosomes के बिना spindle organise कर लेते हैं; इसलिए animal जैसा aster arrangement जरूरी नहीं। Rigid cell wall के कारण plant cell pinching नहीं करता: बीच में बनी cell plate बाहर की ओर बढ़ती है। Animal में contractile ring cell को बाहर से अंदर की ओर कसती है।
beats.on_screen: Plant plate expands outward; animal furrow constricts inward; wall highlighted.

beats.say: Cell plate और cleavage furrow को chromosome separation के नाम मत समझना। ये cytoplasm बाँटने के 2 तरीके हैं। और centrioles वाला contrast typical higher plants के लिए है, हर plant group की हर cell पर लागू नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Do not confuse: mitosis ≠ cytokinesis; typical-cell qualification.

beats.say: एक साथ देखो: plant में centrioles और asters नहीं, cell plate है, division mainly meristems में है। Animal side पर centrioles और asters, cleavage furrow, और कई body tissues में division है। अब meristem को plant-tissue tree में रखेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Four-row plant–animal difference table.

beats.say: पहला आधार है active division: Meristematic tissue नए cells बनाता है; Permanent tissue के cells खास काम के लिए differentiated होते हैं और आम तौर पर actively divide नहीं करते। Permanent tissue में अगला आधार cell types हैं: Simple में मुख्यतः 1 type, Complex में कई types साथ काम करते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Division activity → main split; cell composition → permanent-tissue split.

beats.say: दोनों charts में root Plant Tissues है; नीचे Meristematic और Permanent की 2 मुख्य branches हैं। Meristematic के नीचे Apical, Intercalary और Lateral हैं। Permanent के नीचे Simple और Complex हैं; हर नीचे का नाम अपनी ऊपर वाली branch से जुड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Reveal top two levels of the merged tree.

beats.say: Meristematic branch के 3 types को जगह से पहचानो। Apical meristem root और shoot tips पर length growth से जुड़ा है; Lateral meristem sides पर girth बढ़ाता है। Intercalary meristem mature tissues के बीच, जैसे grasses के leaf या internode bases पर होता है।
beats.on_screen: Plant outline: tips, basal intercalary regions and lateral layers.

beats.say: Simple permanent tissue में Parenchyma, Collenchyma और Sclerenchyma रखो। Page 1 पर ‘Paranchyma’ printed है; page 8 और standard spelling Parenchyma है। Parenchyma के living, relatively thin-walled cells storage जैसे काम करते हैं; इसके नीचे Aerenchyma और Chlorenchyma हैं।
beats.on_screen: Simple branch; printed Paranchyma linked to Parenchyma; two subtypes revealed.

beats.say: Aerenchyma, Parenchyma का large air spaces वाला form है, जो aquatic parts में buoyancy में मदद कर सकता है। Chlorenchyma भी Parenchyma है, लेकिन chloroplasts वाला, photosynthesis के लिए। इन्हें Simple के सीधे बराबर branches नहीं, Parenchyma के नीचे रखो।
beats.on_screen: Air spaces ↔ chloroplasts; both connect to Parenchyma.

beats.say: Collenchyma Simple permanent tissue है: living cells की unevenly thickened walls flexible support देती हैं। Sclerenchyma भी Simple है, लेकिन generally mature cells dead और walls thick, lignified होती हैं। इसलिए growing part का flexible support और mature part की rigidity अलग समझो।
beats.on_screen: Collenchyma: flexible support; Sclerenchyma: thick lignified walls.

beats.say: Sclerenchyma के नीचे Fibres और Sclereids हैं; दूसरे chart में Sclerenchyma fibers लिखा है। Fibres आम तौर पर लंबे, पतले होते हैं; Sclereids छोटे और अलग-अलग shapes के हो सकते हैं। Pear की gritty texture Sclereids का जाना-पहचाना example है।
beats.on_screen: Sclerenchyma → Fibres / Sclerenchyma fibers and Sclereids; elongated versus varied cells.

beats.say: Complex permanent tissue के नीचे Xylem और Phloem हैं। Xylem मुख्यतः water और minerals, Phloem organic food transport करता है। इनके नीचे कई components दिखना समझाता है कि Complex में अलग cell types मिलकर काम करते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Complex → Xylem and Phloem; water/minerals versus organic food.

beats.say: Page 1 के visible Xylem components हैं Tracheids, Vessels, जिन्हें Tracheae भी लिखा है, और Xylem parenchyma। Tracheids और vessel elements conducting cells हैं; vessels में elements end-to-end जुड़ते हैं। Xylem parenchyma living cells से storage और local exchange में मदद करता है।
beats.on_screen: Xylem component box: Tracheids; Vessels (Tracheae); Xylem parenchyma.

beats.say: Visible Phloem components हैं Sieve tubes, Companion cells और Phloem parenchyma। Sieve tubes conducting route देते हैं; Companion cells उनकी functioning में मदद करते हैं। Phloem parenchyma storage और local exchange से इस system को support करता है।
beats.on_screen: Phloem component box: Sieve tubes; Companion cells; Phloem parenchyma.

beats.say: Tree की arrows समय का order नहीं, membership दिखाती हैं। Apical एक meristem type है, Fibres Sclerenchyma का form है, और Sieve tubes Phloem के components हैं; ये एक level के alternatives नहीं। Page 1 के नीचे के boxes cropped हैं, इसलिए visible components को पूरी list मत मानना।

beats.say: पूरा tree जोड़ो: Plant Tissues से Meristematic और Permanent; Meristematic से Apical, Intercalary, Lateral। Permanent से Simple और Complex; Simple से Parenchyma, Collenchyma, Sclerenchyma। Parenchyma के नीचे Aerenchyma और Chlorenchyma; Sclerenchyma के नीचे Fibres और Sclereids; Complex के नीचे Xylem और Phloem, जिनके components अभी जोड़े।

beat.say: Meristematic के नीचे Apical, Intercalary और Lateral हैं। ये तीनों Meristematic tissue के types हैं।

beats.say: Plant की बढ़ती tip और मजबूत पुरानी stem में cells का काम एक जैसा क्यों नहीं होता? कहीं नए cells बनाने हैं, कहीं support देना है। आज division के differences से चलकर इन tissues का पूरा नक्शा जोड़ेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Growing tip and mature stem; division → tissue map.

beats.say: Mitosis और meiosis, दोनों में nucleus के chromosomes daughter cells तक पहुँचते हैं। तुलना में पहले cell का context, फिर divisions और products, फिर chromosome number देखेंगे। केवल 2 और 4 याद करना पूरी समझ नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Common feature: chromosome distribution; comparison criteria appear.

beats.say: Book mitosis को somatic cells, यानी body cells से, और meiosis को germ cells से जोड़ती है। Products के काम में mitosis से somatic organs बनते हैं; meiosis को gamete formation से जोड़ा गया है। इसे शुरुआती तुलना समझो, हर life cycle का पूरा नियम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Somatic cells/body formation ↔ germ cells/reproductive association.

beats.say: Mitosis में nucleus 1 बार divide होता है और आम तौर पर 2 daughter cells बनते हैं। Meiosis में 2 nuclear divisions, meiosis I और meiosis II, से आम तौर पर 4 products बनते हैं। यानी इस तुलना में meiotic products की गिनती दोगुनी है।
beats.on_screen: Mitosis: 1 → 2; meiosis: 1 → 2 → 4.

beats.say: Book mitotic daughters को diploid और meiotic daughters को haploid कहती है। Diploid में 2 chromosome sets, यानी 2n; haploid में 1 set, यानी n होता है। Mitosis में starting chromosome number बचता है, meiosis में आधा रह जाता है।
beats.on_screen: Diploid starting cell: mitosis 2n → 2n; meiosis 2n → n.

beats.say: Frequency में book mitosis को more frequent और meiosis को less frequent बताती है। कोई rate या numerical difference नहीं दिया है। Phases में mitosis का prophase, metaphase, anaphase और telophase 1-1 बार आता है; meiosis में हर phase 2 बार, और prophase I के 5 sub-phases हैं।
beats.on_screen: Qualitative frequency contrast; one phase sequence versus I and II; prophase I: 5 subdivisions.

beats.say: Crossing over को table mitosis में absent और meiosis में present दिखाती है। इसमें paired homologous chromosomes की non-sister chromatids के बीच corresponding DNA segments exchange होते हैं। यह meiosis के prophase I की घटना है, जिससे नए allele combinations बन सकते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Paired homologues exchange matching segments; introductory mitosis/meiosis contrast.

beats.say: इन differences की वजह separation का तरीका है। Meiosis I में homologous partners अलग होते हैं, इसलिए sets आधे होते हैं; meiosis II में sister chromatids अलग होती हैं। Mitosis starting ploidy बचाता है, इसलिए diploid parent से diploid, लेकिन haploid parent से haploid daughters भी बन सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Homologues separate in I; sister chromatids separate in II; mitosis preserves starting ploidy.

beats.say: Growth और cell replacement में बार-बार mitosis चाहिए; meiosis खास reproductive stages से जुड़ा है। Germ-line cells भी mitosis कर सकती हैं। Land plants में meiosis सीधे gametes नहीं, spores बनाता है; उनसे बने gametophytes mitosis से gametes बनाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Growth/replacement; land plants: meiosis → spores → gametophyte → gametes by mitosis.

beats.say: सबसे जरूरी confusion: chromosome number और DNA amount अलग हैं। Printed row mitosis की शुरुआत में chromosome doubling, और meiosis I के बाद doubling का दावा करती है; यह सही mechanism नहीं है। DNA S phase में mitosis से पहले और meiosis I से पहले copy होता है, meiosis I और II के बीच नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Printed row flagged incorrect; DNA replication → mitosis OR meiosis I → meiosis II, with no intervening replication.

beats.say: DNA copying से sister chromatids बनती हैं; centromeres से गिने जाने वाला chromosome number उसी समय दोगुना नहीं होता। Book का ‘Equation division’ standard term equational division के लिए है। Mitosis equational है; meiosis overall reduction division है, लेकिन meiosis I reductional और meiosis II equational है।
beats.on_screen: DNA amount ≠ chromosome number; Equation [printed] → equational [standard].

beats.say: Table को अब पढ़ो: mitosis में 1 division, 2 daughters, chromosome number वही; meiosis में 2 divisions, 4 products, number आधा। Phases का 1 set बनाम 2 sets, और usual crossing-over contrast भी साथ रखो। DNA replication वाली printed row को सही sequence से बदलकर समझना है।
beats.on_screen: Comparison table with all taught criteria; incorrect replication row replaced by corrected sequence.

beats.say: अब plant और animal cells की तुलना में दोनों तरफ mitosis ही है। दोनों को chromosomes बाँटने हैं और cytoplasm अलग करना है। Nucleus का division mitosis है; cytoplasm बाँटना cytokinesis है।
beats.on_screen: Shared tasks: nuclear division and cytokinesis, labelled separately.

beats.say: Table में plants की तरफ centrioles absent, animals की तरफ present हैं। Asters भी plants में नहीं, animals में बनते हैं। Aster को centrosomal region से फैलती star-like microtubules की arrangement समझो।
beats.on_screen: Typical plant versus animal spindle; animal centriole and aster highlighted.

beats.say: Cytokinesis में plant cell cell plate बनाता है; animal cell में furrowing और cytoplasm का cleavage होता है। Division की जगह भी अलग दिखाई गई है: plants में mainly meristem, animals में body के अलग-अलग tissues। Mainly का मतलब केवल वहीं नहीं, और throughout का मतलब हर cell नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Cell plate ↔ cleavage furrow; meristems ↔ distributed dividing tissues.

beats.say: Typical higher-plant cells centrioles वाले centrosomes के बिना spindle organise कर लेते हैं; इसलिए animal जैसा aster arrangement जरूरी नहीं। Rigid cell wall के कारण plant cell pinching नहीं करता: बीच में बनी cell plate बाहर की ओर बढ़ती है। Animal में contractile ring cell को बाहर से अंदर की ओर कसती है।
beats.on_screen: Plant plate expands outward; animal furrow constricts inward; wall highlighted.

beats.say: Cell plate और cleavage furrow को chromosome separation के नाम मत समझना। ये cytoplasm बाँटने के 2 तरीके हैं। और centrioles वाला contrast typical higher plants के लिए है, हर plant group की हर cell पर लागू नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Do not confuse: mitosis ≠ cytokinesis; typical-cell qualification.

beats.say: एक साथ देखो: plant में centrioles और asters नहीं, cell plate है, division mainly meristems में है। Animal side पर centrioles और asters, cleavage furrow, और कई body tissues में division है। अब meristem को plant-tissue tree में रखेंगे।

beats.say: Intercalary meristem भी Meristematic tissue है। यह Apical की तरह terminal tip पर नहीं, mature tissues के बीच होता है, जैसे grasses के leaf या internode bases पर।
beats.on_screen: Highlight basal intercalary regions; compare all three meristem positions.

beats.say: Simple permanent tissue में Parenchyma, Collenchyma और Sclerenchyma रखो। ये तीनों इसी branch के tissue types हैं।
beats.on_screen: Simple permanent tissue → Parenchyma, Collenchyma, Sclerenchyma.

beats.say: Page 1 पर ‘Paranchyma’ printed है; page 8 और standard spelling Parenchyma है। यह Simple permanent tissue है, जिसके living, relatively thin-walled cells storage जैसे काम करते हैं। इसके नीचे Aerenchyma और Chlorenchyma हैं।
beats.on_screen: Paranchyma [page 1] → Parenchyma; reveal Aerenchyma and Chlorenchyma.

beats.say: Aerenchyma, Parenchyma का large air spaces वाला form है, जो aquatic parts में buoyancy में मदद कर सकता है। Chlorenchyma भी Parenchyma है, लेकिन chloroplasts वाला, photosynthesis के लिए। इन्हें Simple के सीधे बराबर branches नहीं, Parenchyma के नीचे रखो।
beats.on_screen: Air spaces ↔ chloroplasts; both connect to Parenchyma.

beats.say: Collenchyma Simple permanent tissue है। Living cells की unevenly thickened walls flexible support देती हैं, इसलिए growing parts में support के साथ bending भी हो सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Collenchyma under Simple: living cells, uneven wall thickening, flexible support.

beats.say: Sclerenchyma भी Simple है, लेकिन generally mature cells dead और walls thick, lignified होती हैं। ये walls मजबूती देती हैं। इसलिए Collenchyma का flexible support और Sclerenchyma की rigidity अलग समझो।
beats.on_screen: Sclerenchyma: thick lignified walls; contrast with living, flexible Collenchyma.

beats.say: Sclerenchyma के नीचे Fibres और Sclereids हैं। दूसरे chart में Fibres के लिए Sclerenchyma fibers लिखा है।
beats.on_screen: Sclerenchyma → Fibres / Sclerenchyma fibers and Sclereids.

beats.say: Fibres, यानी इस chart के Sclerenchyma fibers, आम तौर पर लंबे और पतले होते हैं। दोनों labels Sclerenchyma के इसी form को दिखाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight the Fibres branch and an elongated cell.

beats.say: Sclereids भी Sclerenchyma में हैं, लेकिन Fibres के मुकाबले छोटे और अलग-अलग shapes के हो सकते हैं। इनकी thick, lignified walls hardness देती हैं; pear की gritty texture इसका जाना-पहचाना example है।
beats.on_screen: Sclereids: varied short cells; pear texture example.

beats.say: Complex permanent tissue के नीचे Xylem और Phloem हैं। इनके नीचे कई components दिखना समझाता है कि Complex में अलग cell types मिलकर काम करते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Complex permanent tissue → Xylem and Phloem; component branches highlighted.

beats.say: Xylem और Phloem दोनों Complex permanent tissues हैं। Xylem mainly water और minerals transport करता है; Phloem organic food transport करता है।
beats.on_screen: Xylem: water/minerals ↔ Phloem: organic food.

beats.say: Page 1 के visible Xylem components हैं Tracheids, Vessels, जिन्हें Tracheae भी लिखा है, और Xylem parenchyma। Tracheids इसी Xylem के conducting cells हैं।
beats.on_screen: Xylem component box; highlight Tracheids.

beats.say: Vessels, यानी Tracheae, भी Xylem में हैं; इनमें conducting elements end-to-end जुड़ते हैं। Xylem parenchyma इसी tissue के living cells हैं, जो storage और local exchange में मदद करते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight Vessels (Tracheae), then Xylem parenchyma and its storage/exchange role.

beats.say: Visible Phloem components हैं Sieve tubes, Companion cells और Phloem parenchyma। Sieve tubes इसी Phloem में conducting route देते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Phloem component box; highlight Sieve tubes.

beats.say: Companion cells Phloem में Sieve tubes की functioning में मदद करते हैं। Phloem parenchyma भी इसी tissue में है और storage तथा local exchange से system को support करता है। इस तरह components साथ काम करते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Companion cells assist Sieve tubes; Phloem parenchyma provides storage and local exchange.

beats.say: Tree की arrows समय का order नहीं, membership दिखाती हैं। Apical एक meristem type है, Fibres Sclerenchyma का form है, और Sieve tubes Phloem के components हैं; ये एक level के alternatives नहीं। Page 1 के नीचे के boxes cropped हैं, इसलिए visible components को पूरी list मत मानना।
beats.on_screen: Highlight parent–child paths; subtype versus component; cropped-list warning.

beats.say: पूरा tree जोड़ो: Plant Tissues से Meristematic और Permanent; Meristematic से Apical, Intercalary, Lateral। Permanent से Simple और Complex; Simple से Parenchyma, Collenchyma, Sclerenchyma। Parenchyma के नीचे Aerenchyma और Chlorenchyma; Sclerenchyma के नीचे Fibres और Sclereids; Complex के नीचे Xylem और Phloem, जिनके components अभी जोड़े।
beats.on_screen: Complete merged classification tree, including all visible Xylem and Phloem components.

notes.about: This review evaluates script v6, which compares mitosis and meiosis, contrasts plant and animal cytokinesis, and integrates the two plant-tissue classification trees from pages 1 and 8.
key_questions: Does the script cover all 55 required items and answer all book-based and required questions?
Does the narration stay within the 1079–1443 spoken word window required by S2-01?
Do all three parts follow their respective comparison and classification teaching patterns in natural spoken Hinglish?

decisions.decision: Pass the script with zero blocking issues.

problems.fix: Optionally mention the five sub-phase names in b6 or b7 if time permits.

checklist.note: Every statement is accurately sourced from the book or marked as outside/mixed knowledge, and the flawed printed claim in row 9 (p001-i22) and the typo 'Equation division' / 'Paranchyma' are explicitly and accurately addressed.

The explanations are thorough and conceptually sound for UPSC/State PCS aspirants, covering ploidy, homologous vs sister chromatid separation, plant life-cycle qualifications, and the hierarchy of plant tissues.
The maker's notes clearly state what the unit is about, the key pedagogical decisions with their reasons, and the uncertainty regarding cropped boxes on page 1.
The narration is natural, clear spoken Hinglish suitable for a top educator.
No book content is cut short or left as 'etc.'; all 11 mitosis/meiosis rows, 4 plant/animal rows, and every branch and visible component of both plant-tissue trees are explicitly named and taught.
Planned time is 10 minutes and the spoken narration is approximately 1,220 words, which sits squarely inside the required 1,079–1,443 word window (8.3–11.1 minutes at 130 wpm).
The script flows logically from cell division to meristems and permanent tissues, covers all 55 required items, and answers every book question without repetition.
Prerequisite concepts (such as chromosome sets, DNA copying, and nuclear vs cell division) are seamlessly integrated and reminded briefly without exceeding 2 beats.
Hindi is written in Devanagari, technical English terms are in Roman script, sentences are short and spoken, and stiff Sanskritized words have been avoided.
All covers_item_ids and answers claims in the beats are accurate and substantiated by the spoken text.
Every part has a complete frame, follows the 5-step comparison or classification teaching pattern in order, and teaches every assigned card item.
